q: 1. An agreement between two parties or more to do or not to do any work is known as:
explain: By legal definition, a contract is an agreement enforceable by law between two or more parties creating mutual obligations.

q: 2. *An EPC contract means :
explain: EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement, and Construction, often referred to as a turnkey contract.

q: 3. A written offer submitted by contractors to execute certain work at certain rates within a fixed time is called:
explain: A tender is an official written invitation response offering to perform construction works under stated rates and schedules.

q: 4. Force Majeure in a contract is:
options: Occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
Preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure encompasses both the occurrence of an uncontrollable event and its effect of preventing both parties from performing their obligations - both A and B.

q: 5. The document announcing to prospective bidders that the owner is ready to receive the bids is called:
explain: An Invitation for Bids (IFB) or Notice to Bidders publicly notifies qualified contractors that an employer is accepting bids for a project.

q: 6. Acquisition of land for any construction should be perfomed :
explain: To prevent site possession disputes and contract delays, land acquisition and right-of-way clearances must be secured prior to issuing tender notices.

q: 7. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: When general or standard specifications fall short for unique requirements, performance or special technical specifications are appended.

q: 8. Which of the following is not Bid document?
explain: The Letter of Acceptance (LOA) is issued after evaluation during award stage; it is not a part of the original issued bidding documents.

q: 9. An offer in writing to execute some specified civil works at certain rates within a fixed time under certain conditions of contract is called :
explain: A bid (or tender) is the formal written offer submitted by a contractor in response to an invitation to work.

q: 10. An EPC contract means:
explain: EPC stands for Engineering, Procurement, and Construction—a form of turnkey agreement where one contractor handles total delivery.

q: 11. The supplementary specification prepared and applied if the standard specification does not cover the requirement of works under a contract is called:
explain: The answer key indicates 'performance specification', though in many contexts, these are also referred to as 'special specifications'.

q: 12. A contractor's role in construction includes:
explain: Maintaining safety at the construction site is a core responsibility of the contractor, unlike payment/certification which are the client/engineer's roles.

q: 13. Earnest money is a ........ towards the execution of a publicly tender government contract.
explain: Earnest money is a security deposit made to guarantee bid commitment during public tender procedures.

q: 14. Which of the followings should be practiced first if a dispute arises in a contract?
explain: Amicable settlement (direct negotiation between parties) is typically the first step attempted before escalating to mediation, adjudication, or arbitration.

q: 15. The document giving the information about the tender, prequalification, contractor, construction, procurement of materials and services is called
explain: The tender document (or bid document) contains all the necessary information for a contractor to prepare a bid.

q: 16. Force majeure in contract is:
options: occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure covers unforeseeable extraordinary events beyond reasonable control (such as natural disasters or war) that prevent contract fulfillment.

q: 17. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement refers to a dispute being resolved directly and mutually by the two contracting parties themselves, without external intervention.

q: 18. "Fraudulent Practice" means
options: The offering, giving, receiving of anything of value of influence the action of a public official in the procurement process
Misrepresentation of facts to influence a procurement process
explain: Fraudulent practice covers both improper inducement of officials and misrepresentation of facts - both a and b.

q: 19. Contractor's prequalification is required for:
explain: Prequalification is required specifically for major and specialized works needing verified contractor capability.

q: 20. Time extension may need to be granted due to
explain: Time extensions can be warranted by force majeure events as well as delays caused by the purchaser/employer - both a and b.

q: 21. While filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers
explain: A contractor considers site conditions, material availability, and labour availability while preparing a tender bid - all of the above.

q: 22. A surety bond issued by an insurance company or a bank that provides legal guarantee to the owner or employer that the bidder will sign the contract if it is awarded to him is called
explain: Bid security is the surety bond guaranteeing that the successful bidder will sign the contract if awarded.

q: 23. When actual cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor then such a contract is known as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor actual costs incurred plus an agreed percentage as profit.

q: 24. A contractor can start the construction works with following the receipt of
explain: The 'notice to proceed' is the formal authorization document that allows the contractor to commence construction works.
